title: Daily Life - Talking About Relatives

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and we're going to a family party today, right Marco?
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，我们今天要去参加一个家庭聚会，对吧，马可？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: We're going to go see our family, our relatives and we're going to talk about all the different family members that you can have.
segments.zh: 我们要去看我们的家人，我们的亲戚，我们将谈论你可以拥有的所有不同的家庭成员。

segments.en: So, there are some very, very specific family members that sometimes you don't really know the names of.
segments.zh: 所以，有一些非常非常具体的家庭成员有时你并不真正知道他们的名字。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So, we're not talking about mother, father, brother, sister.
segments.zh: 所以，我们不是在谈论母亲、父亲、兄弟、姐妹。

segments.en: We're talking about what we call in English extended family.
segments.zh: 我们要谈的是英语里所说的“大家庭”（extended family）。

segments.en: So, that means not just the people you live with but also people you're related to who are maybe in different parts of your family.
segments.zh: 所以，这不仅指和你住在一起的人，也指和你有亲属关系、可能属于你家族其他分支的人。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So, let's listen to our dialogue and we'll be back in a bit.
segments.zh: 所以，让我们听听我们的对话，我们会回来的。

segments.en: What are you doing this weekend?
segments.zh: 这个周末你在做什么？

segments.en: My brother-in-law is having a small get-together at his house and he invited me.
segments.zh: 我姐夫要在家办个小聚会，邀请了我。

segments.en: Is it a family thing or just friends?
segments.zh: 是家人聚会，还是朋友聚会？

segments.en: A bit of both.
segments.zh: 家人和朋友都有。

segments.en: Some cousins, aunts and uncles will be there but also some friends from the neighborhood.
segments.zh: 几个表兄弟姐妹、叔叔阿姨，还有一些街坊朋友。

segments.en: Is your great-uncle Rick going to be there?
segments.zh: 你舅爷爷瑞克也会来吗？

segments.en: He is really funny.
segments.zh: 他真的很幽默。

segments.en: Yeah, he's going to be there with his stepson and his ex-wife.
segments.zh: 会，他会带着继子和前妻一起来。

segments.en: You mean your sister?
segments.zh: 你是说你姐姐吗？

segments.en: No, Rick is actually my great-uncle so he's my grandmother's brother.
segments.zh: 不，瑞克是我的舅爷爷，也就是我奶奶的兄弟。

segments.en: You lost me.
segments.zh: 我没听懂。

segments.en: I'll explain later.
segments.zh: 回头再给你解释。

segments.en: Let's go.
segments.zh: 我们走吧。

segments.en: Alright, so now let's talk about these family members on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 好吧，现在让我们谈谈这些家庭成员的语言要点。

segments.en: Language Takeaway
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: So, Marco, we've got four family members to talk about today.
segments.zh: 所以，马可，我们今天有四个家庭成员要谈。

segments.en: And the first one is brother-in-law.
segments.zh: 第一个是姐夫。

segments.en: Right, so we have the word brother-in-law.
segments.zh: 对，所以我们有姐夫这个词。

segments.en: So, basically this person is married to your sister.
segments.zh: 所以基本上，这个人是和你姐姐（或妹妹）结了婚。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So, I have a brother, I have a sister.
segments.zh: 所以，我有一个兄弟，我有一个妹妹。

segments.en: But when these people marry, they marry someone who I'm not related to by blood.
segments.zh: 但是当这些人结婚时，他们会和某个与我没有血缘关系的人结婚。

segments.en: We call them in-laws, so brother-in-law, sister-in-law.
segments.zh: 我们称他们为姻亲，所以姐夫，嫂子。

segments.en: Right, so that's exactly it.
segments.zh: 没错，就是这样。

segments.en: The key there is that when it has the ending in-law, it means that you're not related to them by blood.
segments.zh: 关键在于，当它以 in-law 结尾时，就说明你与他们没有血缘关系。

segments.en: It's your extended family because of marriage.
segments.zh: 这是因婚姻而结成的大家庭。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So, I have a younger brother.
segments.zh: 所以，我有一个弟弟。

segments.en: When he gets married, I will have a sister-in-law.
segments.zh: 等他结婚，我就有了一个嫂子。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And it applies to, for example, father-in-law.
segments.zh: 例如，它也适用于 father-in-law（岳父、公公）。

segments.en: That would be your husband's dad or mother-in-law would be your husband's mother.
segments.zh: 那指的是你丈夫的父亲（公公），而 mother-in-law 就是你丈夫的母亲（婆婆）。

segments.en: Yeah, so these are all related to you by marriage.
segments.zh: 是的，所以这些都是通过婚姻与你有关的。

segments.en: All right, so now moving on to the next type of extended family member that we have is a stepson.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以现在继续我们拥有的下一个类型的大家庭成员是继子。

segments.en: Your uncle has a stepson.
segments.zh: 你叔叔有继子。

segments.en: So, a stepson.
segments.zh: 所以，一个继子。

segments.en: Now, this can get very confusing.
segments.zh: 现在，这可能会变得非常混乱。

segments.en: Let's take a simple, simple family.
segments.zh: 让我们以一个简单、简单的家庭为例。

segments.en: We have two people and they're married.
segments.zh: 我们有两个人，他们结婚了。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And then they get divorced, so they split up.
segments.zh: 然后他们离婚了，所以他们分手了。

segments.en: And now maybe they had some kids.
segments.zh: 现在也许他们有一些孩子。

segments.en: The wife has kids, and she gets married to someone else.
segments.zh: 妻子有孩子，她嫁给了别人。

segments.en: So, her new husband calls her son his stepson.
segments.zh: 所以，她的新丈夫称她的儿子为他的继子。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Because it's not his son.
segments.zh: 因为这不是他的儿子。

segments.en: It's another man's son.
segments.zh: 这是另一个男人的儿子。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: But they're still related by marriage.
segments.zh: 但他们仍然与婚姻有关。

segments.en: So, when your new husband or your new wife has kids from another marriage, they're called stepson, stepdaughter.
segments.zh: 所以，当你的新丈夫或新婚妻子带着前一段婚姻的孩子时，这些孩子就叫继子、继女。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So, it's the same thing as if my mother got divorced and she remarried.
segments.zh: 所以，这就好比如果我妈妈离了婚又再婚。

segments.en: She has a new husband.
segments.zh: 她有一个新丈夫。

segments.en: That man would be my stepfather.
segments.zh: 那个人会是我的继父。

segments.en: All right, so these are all family members.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这些都是家庭成员。

segments.en: When you hear the word step, family members that we have because of divorce.
segments.zh: 当你听到 step 这个词时，指的就是因离婚而形成的家庭成员。

segments.en: So, stepson, stepdaughter, stepfather, stepmother.
segments.zh: 所以，继子，继女，继父，继母。

segments.en: All right, and now, again, related to the whole divorce thing, the person that you get divorced to is called an ex-wife or an ex-husband.
segments.zh: 好吧，现在还是和离婚有关，和你离婚的那个人就叫做前妻或前夫。

segments.en: All right, so ex, like ex-girlfriend or ex-boyfriend means previous.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以 ex，比如 ex-girlfriend 或 ex-boyfriend，表示“以前的”。

segments.en: So, my ex-wife is someone I was married to before or in the case of a woman, my ex-husband was someone I was married to before, but we got divorced.
segments.zh: 所以，我的前妻就是我以前结婚的对象；对一个女人来说，我的前夫就是我以前结婚的对象，只不过我们离婚了。

segments.en: So, we're not married now.
segments.zh: 所以，我们现在没有结婚。

segments.en: That's exactly it.
segments.zh: 正是如此。

segments.en: So, it only applies to husband and wife, right?
segments.zh: 所以，它只适用于夫妻，对吧？

segments.en: You don't say my ex-children or my ex-mother-in-law.
segments.zh: 你不要说我的前孩子或我的前岳母。

segments.en: Well, because your children are always your children.
segments.zh: 好吧，因为你的孩子永远是你的孩子。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: If you talk about your ex-wife's parents, you just say my ex-wife's father or my ex-wife's mother because there's no more in-law.
segments.zh: 如果你谈论你前妻的父母，你就说我前妻的父亲或我前妻的母亲，因为已经不再是姻亲关系了。

segments.en: There's no law.
segments.zh: 没有法律。

segments.en: You're not married.
segments.zh: 你没有结婚。

segments.en: Right, okay.
segments.zh: 对，好。

segments.en: And lastly, now we have an uncle, but just not any uncle.
segments.zh: 最后，现在要讲一个叔叔，但不是普通意义上的叔叔。

segments.en: We have our great uncle.
segments.zh: 我们要讲 great uncle（舅爷爷、伯祖父）。

segments.en: Great uncle.
segments.zh: 舅爷爷；伯祖父。

segments.en: So, they actually explain this in the dialogue.
segments.zh: 所以，他们实际上在对话中解释了这一点。

segments.en: They say, he is my grandmother's brother.
segments.zh: 他们说，他是我祖母的兄弟。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Okay, so my uncle, this is simple.
segments.zh: 好吧，我的叔叔，这很简单。

segments.en: My uncle is my mother's brother or my father's brother.
segments.zh: 我的叔叔是我母亲的兄弟或我父亲的兄弟。

segments.en: Easy.
segments.zh: 简单。

segments.en: But my great uncle is one of my grandparent's brothers.
segments.zh: 但我的 great uncle（舅爷爷、伯祖父）是我祖父母中某一位的兄弟。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So, my grandmother's brother or my grandfather's brother.
segments.zh: 所以，我祖母的兄弟或我祖父的兄弟。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: In English, we don't distinguish.
segments.zh: 在英语中，我们不区分。

segments.en: We don't say a different word for grandmother's brother or grandfather's brother.
segments.zh: 我们不会对祖母的兄弟或祖父的兄弟说不同的词。

segments.en: Right, right, exactly.
segments.zh: 没错，没错。

segments.en: So, your great uncle could be either your grandmother's brother or your grandfather's brother.
segments.zh: 所以，你的 great uncle（舅爷爷、伯祖父）可能是你祖母的兄弟，也可能是你祖父的兄弟。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So, in my family, I have, well, I just have one great uncle and one great aunt.
segments.zh: 所以，在我家，我只有一位舅爷爷和一位姑奶奶。

segments.en: My grandmother has a sister, so I have a great aunt, and my grandfather has a brother, so I have a great uncle.
segments.zh: 我祖母有一个姐妹，所以我有一位姑奶奶；我祖父有一个兄弟，所以我有一位舅爷爷。

segments.en: And now, the prefix great can also be applied, for example, to grandparents.
segments.zh: 现在，前缀 great 也可以应用于祖父母。

segments.en: So, you can say, my great grandfather.
segments.zh: 所以，你可以说，我的曾祖父。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So, we're talking about generations.
segments.zh: 所以，我们谈论的是几代人。

segments.en: I have a grandfather, but his father is my great grandfather.
segments.zh: 我有一个祖父，但他的父亲是我的曾祖父。

segments.en: That means we go back in the past one more generation.
segments.zh: 这意味着又往前追溯了一代人。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: All right, so let's take a break and let's listen to the dialogue again.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们休息一下，让我们再听一次对话。

segments.en: What are you doing this weekend?
segments.zh: 这个周末你在做什么？

segments.en: My brother-in-law is having a small get-together at his house, and he invited me.
segments.zh: 我的姐夫在他家有一个小聚会，他邀请了我。

segments.en: Is it a family thing or just friends?
segments.zh: 是家人聚会，还是朋友聚会？

segments.en: A bit of both.
segments.zh: 家人和朋友都有。

segments.en: Some cousins, aunts, and uncles will be there, but also some friends from the neighborhood.
segments.zh: 一些表亲、阿姨和叔叔会在那里，但也有一些附近的朋友。

segments.en: Is your great uncle Rick going to be there?
segments.zh: 你的舅爷爷瑞克会在那儿吗？

segments.en: He is really funny.
segments.zh: 他真的很幽默。

segments.en: Yeah, he's going to be there with his stepson and his ex-wife.
segments.zh: 会，他会带着继子和前妻一起来。

segments.en: You mean your sister?
segments.zh: 你是说你姐姐吗？

segments.en: No, Rick is actually my great uncle, so he's my grandmother's brother.
segments.zh: 不，瑞克其实是我的舅爷爷，所以他是我祖母的兄弟。

segments.en: You lost me.
segments.zh: 我没听懂。

segments.en: I'll explain later.
segments.zh: 回头再给你解释。

segments.en: Let's go.
segments.zh: 我们走吧。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So, we've picked out three key phrases for you.
segments.zh: 因此，我们为您挑选了三个关键短语。

segments.en: Let's take a look at those now on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 现在我们在流利表达里来看看这些短语。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: All right, so on Fluency Builder, we have a great noun here, actually.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以在流利表达上，我们实际上有一个很棒的名词。

segments.en: You might have heard this before in a different way, but in today's dialogue, we're talking about a small get-together.
segments.zh: 您可能以前以不同的方式听说过这一点，但在今天的对话中，我们谈论的是一个小小的聚会。

segments.en: My brother-in-law is having a small get-together.
segments.zh: 我的姐夫要办个小聚会。

segments.en: Now, what is a get-together, Mark?
segments.zh: 现在，什么是聚会，马克？

segments.en: Right, so as you notice, we say a get-together, meaning that get-together, we are taking it as a noun.
segments.zh: 对，正如您注意到的那样，我们说的是聚会，这意味着聚会，我们将其视为名词。

segments.en: And it may be confusing because you see the verb get, right?
segments.zh: 它可能会令人困惑，因为你看到了动词 GET，对吧？

segments.en: And you're thinking it's a verb, but no.
segments.zh: 你认为这是一个动词，但不是。

segments.en: A get-together is a reunion, a meeting.
segments.zh: get-together 就是一次团聚、一次会面。

segments.en: All right, a party.
segments.zh: 好吧，一个聚会。

segments.en: A party.
segments.zh: 一个聚会。

segments.en: So, maybe it's a very informal party, very casual.
segments.zh: 所以，也许这是一个非常非正式的派对，非常随意。

segments.en: Not fancy.
segments.zh: 不讲究；不花哨。

segments.en: A get-together.
segments.zh: 一个聚会。

segments.en: I could say, Marco, I'm having a get-together at my apartment.
segments.zh: 我可以说，马可，我要在我的公寓聚会。

segments.en: Do you want to come and bring your girlfriend?
segments.zh: 你想来带你的女朋友吗？

segments.en: Right, so very simple.
segments.zh: 对，非常简单。

segments.en: Maybe we have a drink or some food, but it's nothing fancy.
segments.zh: 也许我们会喝点东西、吃点东西，但没什么讲究。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Very informal, very casual.
segments.zh: 非常随意，非常随意。

segments.en: A get-together.
segments.zh: 一个聚会。

segments.en: And when we were asking about the get-together, we asked if it's a family thing or is it just friends?
segments.zh: 当我们询问聚会时，我们问这是家庭的事情还是只是朋友？

segments.en: So, I want to take a look at this phrase here, a family thing.
segments.zh: 所以，我想来看看这个短语，a family thing（家庭场合）。

segments.en: Is it a family thing?
segments.zh: 是家庭的事情吗？

segments.en: What am I asking when I say, okay, Marco, this party you're having, is it a family thing?
segments.zh: 当我说，好吧，马可，你举办的这个派对时，我在问什么，这是家庭的事情吗？

segments.en: Well, you're asking if it's a family reunion, a family party.
segments.zh: 好吧，你在问它是否是家庭聚会，一个家庭聚会。

segments.en: So, that means if I'm not in your family, can I still come?
segments.zh: 所以，那意思是说，如果我不是你的家人，我还能来吗？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Right, because if it's a family thing, it's just for people in my family.
segments.zh: 是的，因为如果这是一个家庭的事情，它只是为了我家里的人。

segments.en: Right, right.
segments.zh: 对，对。

segments.en: If it's for everyone, no problem.
segments.zh: 如果是给大家的，没问题。

segments.en: But I don't want to go to your house if it's a family thing because that's private.
segments.zh: 但如果这是家庭的事情，我不想去你家，因为那是私人的。

segments.en: Right, so usually, for example, maybe Christmas dinner would usually be a family thing.
segments.zh: 是的，所以通常，例如，也许圣诞节晚餐通常是家庭的事情。

segments.en: You celebrate it with your family mostly, but it's not always a family thing.
segments.zh: 你主要是和家人一起庆祝，但这并不总是家庭的事情。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: I could say, this year my birthday is just a family thing.
segments.zh: 我可以说，今年我的生日只是一个家庭的事情。

segments.en: I'm only inviting family members.
segments.zh: 我只是邀请家人。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: All right, and lastly, we got a little bit confused with the great uncle and the stepson and the ex-wife.
segments.zh: 好吧，最后，我们对 great uncle、继子和前妻有点困惑。

segments.en: And so, we said, you know what?
segments.zh: 所以，我们说，你知道吗？

segments.en: You lost me.
segments.zh: 我没听懂。

segments.en: You lost me.
segments.zh: 我没听懂。

segments.en: You lost me.
segments.zh: 我没听懂。

segments.en: Now, this is another great phrase.
segments.zh: 现在，这又是一个很棒的短语。

segments.en: The phrase means, I don't understand.
segments.zh: 这句话的意思是，我不明白。

segments.en: I'm confused.
segments.zh: 我很困惑。

segments.en: Right, that's exactly it.
segments.zh: 没错，就是这样。

segments.en: So, if someone is explaining something and I don't understand, then you can say, you know what?
segments.zh: 所以，如果有人在解释某事而我不明白，那么你可以说，你知道吗？

segments.en: You lost me.
segments.zh: 我没听懂。

segments.en: I don't understand.
segments.zh: 我不明白。

segments.en: Right, and sometimes I say this when someone is giving a very long explanation for something.
segments.zh: 对，有时我会在有人对某事给出很长的解释时这么说。

segments.en: So, to get to my house, you turn left here and then you go two blocks, you turn right and you go straight and you wait for the stoplight.
segments.zh: 所以，要到我家，你在这里左转，然后你走了两个街区，你右转，你直行，你等待着红绿灯。

segments.en: And then you go to the right-hand corner, there's a store.
segments.zh: 然后你去右边的角落，有一家商店。

segments.en: I say, wait, wait, wait.
segments.zh: 我说，等等，等等，等等。

segments.en: You lost me.
segments.zh: 我没听懂。

segments.en: Right, exactly.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: I don't understand.
segments.zh: 我不明白。

segments.en: I'm confused.
segments.zh: 我很困惑。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: All right, so that's all we have.
segments.zh: 好吧，这就是我们所拥有的一切。

segments.en: Let's listen to the dialogue one last time.
segments.zh: 我们最后再听一遍对话。

segments.en: What are you doing this weekend?
segments.zh: 这个周末你在做什么？

segments.en: My brother-in-law is having a small get-together at his house and he invited me.
segments.zh: 我姐夫要在家办个小聚会，邀请了我。

segments.en: Is it a family thing or just friends?
segments.zh: 是家人聚会，还是朋友聚会？

segments.en: A bit of both.
segments.zh: 家人和朋友都有。

segments.en: Some cousins, aunts and uncles will be there, but also some friends from the neighborhood.
segments.zh: 一些表亲、阿姨和叔叔会在那里，但也有一些附近的朋友。

segments.en: Is your great-uncle Rick going to be there?
segments.zh: 你舅爷爷瑞克也会来吗？

segments.en: He is really funny.
segments.zh: 他真的很幽默。

segments.en: Yeah, he's going to be there with his stepson and his ex-wife.
segments.zh: 会，他会带着继子和前妻一起来。

segments.en: You mean your sister?
segments.zh: 你是说你姐姐吗？

segments.en: No, Rick is actually my great-uncle, so he's my grandmother's brother.
segments.zh: 不，瑞克其实是我的舅爷爷，所以他是我祖母的兄弟。

segments.en: You lost me.
segments.zh: 我没听懂。

segments.en: I'll explain later.
segments.zh: 回头再给你解释。

segments.en: Let's go.
segments.zh: 我们走吧。

segments.en: So, speaking of extended family members, what else can we mention?
segments.zh: 那么，说到大家庭成员，我们还能提到什么？

segments.en: We have stepfamily, your stepson, your stepdaughter.
segments.zh: 我们有 stepfamily（继亲家庭），你的继子、继女。

segments.en: What about if you have an adopted child?
segments.zh: 如果你有一个收养的孩子怎么办？

segments.en: Would you differentiate it?
segments.zh: 你会区分它吗？

segments.en: Some people do, some people don't.
segments.zh: 有些人会区分，有些人不会。

segments.en: Most people just say, this is my son, this is my daughter.
segments.zh: 大多数人只是说，这是我的儿子，这是我的女儿。

segments.en: But I would like to add that with stepson, stepdaughter, it's not just divorce that we have this.
segments.zh: 但我想补充一点，继子、继女这种情况并不只是离婚造成的。

segments.en: Also, if the parent, maybe the mother dies and the father has a new wife, then the new wife can say, this is my stepson, this is my stepdaughter.
segments.zh: 还有，如果父母，也许母亲死了，父亲有了新妻子，那么新妻子可以说，这是我的继子，这是我的继女。

segments.en: So, there are two possibilities.
segments.zh: 所以，有两种可能性。

segments.en: One is death and one is remarriage because of divorce.
segments.zh: 一是死亡，一是因离婚而再婚。

segments.en: But as far as adopted, no, usually just say my son and my daughter.
segments.zh: 但就收养而言，不，通常只说我的儿子和我的女儿。

segments.en: But I can tell you this.
segments.zh: 但我可以告诉你这一点。

segments.en: If my father and my mother divorce, my father has a new wife, and together they have a baby, the baby, boy or girl, is my half-brother or half-sister because we share one parent, my father.
segments.zh: 如果我父亲和我的母亲离婚，我父亲有了一个新妻子，他们一起生了一个孩子，这孩子不管是男孩还是女孩，都是我同父异母的兄弟姐妹，因为我们共有一个父母——我的父亲。

segments.en: Right. This is very interesting.
segments.zh: 对。 这很有趣。

segments.en: So, if you do have a brother or sister that is not from your same mother or father, but just one parent, then yeah, it's called a half-brother or sister.
segments.zh: 所以，如果你的兄弟姐妹不是同父同母，而是只共有其中一个父母，那么是的，他/她就被称为 half-brother 或 half-sister（同父异母或同母异父的兄弟姐妹）。

segments.en: Half, remember this, half because half of their parents are the same as your parents.
segments.zh: 一半，记住这一点，一半是因为他们的父母有一半和你父母一样。

segments.en: Maybe one father or mother.
segments.zh: 也许是一位父亲或母亲。

segments.en: But with stepbrothers and stepsisters, the only reason you're related is because of marriage, not because of blood.
segments.zh: 但对于继兄弟和继姐妹，你们有亲属关系的唯一原因是婚姻，而不是血缘。

segments.en: Right. We didn't mention that you could have a stepbrother.
segments.zh: 对。 我们没有提到你可以有一个继兄弟。

segments.en: So, it's your brother, but he's legally your brother, but he's not related to your father or anyone in your family.
segments.zh: 所以，这是你的兄弟，但他在法律上是你的兄弟，但他与你的父亲或你家里的任何人都没有关系。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So, maybe you have many stepbrothers.
segments.zh: 所以，也许你有很多继兄弟。

segments.en: You could have a stepbrother and a half-brother.
segments.zh: 你可以有一个继兄弟和一个同父异母的兄弟。

segments.en: So, there are lots of different combinations because of many different reasons.
segments.zh: 因此，由于许多不同的原因，有很多不同的组合。

segments.en: All right, guys.
segments.zh: 好了，各位。

segments.zh: 今天的时间就到这里。

segments.zh: 但这有点令人困惑的话题。
